name: Tata Steel Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest steel group by capacity (~Tata Steel India ~23 Mt with Jamshedpur, Kalinganagar, Angul/Neelachal, NINL) plus Tata Steel Netherlands (IJmuiden) and UK (Port Talbot, in transition to EAF) and Southeast Asian assets. Captive iron ore and ~45% captive coking coal in India. Q1 FY27 sales Rs60,794 cr, EBITDA Rs9,264 cr (15%), PAT Rs2,385 cr. TTM sales Rs239,756 cr, EBITDA Rs36,189 cr, net profit Rs11,264 cr; market cap Rs2.26 lakh cr. Q2 FY27 results due in November (date unconfirmed); Q2 India crude steel output +10% YoY (6.21 Mt reported 2026-10-07/08).

exposures.mechanism: India ~62% of revenue (~Rs130-140k cr, model estimate) and ~70% of EBITDA; +7% price on ~Rs135k cr = Rs9.5k cr vs TTM EBITDA Rs36,189 cr => +26%; EV/MCap ~1.4 (net debt ~Rs80k cr, model estimate), persistence 0.3 => +11; trimmed for cost co-movement and contract pricing => ~8. Pack: global HRC +0.94 (t=+1.3).

evidence.note: Reuters: Indian steel prices set to rise further

exposures.mechanism: Europe (NL+UK, ~30% of revenue, ~Rs72k cr) prices follow global/EU HRC; +10% global HRC => ~+5% European realisation => ~+Rs3.6k cr = +10% EBITDA x1.4 x0.3 = +4.2, halved for contract lags and EU quota/CBAM dampening => ~+2.

evidence.note: Business Standard: EU quota window for India

exposures.mechanism: India coking coal ~45% captive (Jharia, model knowledge) so ~55% imported; Europe fully imported. Net exposed ~Rs35k cr (~17% of costs): +15% => -14.8% EBITDA; ~40% passed through => -8.9%; x1.4 x0.3 => ~-3.7.

evidence.note: Reuters: coking coal rise squeezes mills

exposures.mechanism: India is ~fully captive (Odisha/Jharkhand mines): higher ore price raises opportunity value and steel prices more than cost; Europe buys ore (~10% of costs there) => net slightly positive/neutral. Pack +1.97 (t=+1.5).
Weaker yuan makes Chinese steel exports cheaper, pressuring Indian and European HRC (path partly in F_STEEL_*). Empirical -4.77 (t=-2.9) shrunk by ~half to avoid double counting.

Europe EBITDA has high operating leverage; +1pp EU growth => +1.5% volume => ~+Rs380 cr (1% EBITDA) x1.4 x0.5 => ~+0.7; plus pricing => ~+1.2. Dutch decarbonisation timetable (joint LoI extended to March 2027) and CBAM add policy risk.

evidence.note: Business Standard: LoI extended; Economic Times: extended to March 2027

exposures.mechanism: European operations use gas and power (~8% of European costs); +15% gas => ~-1.5% Europe EBITDA => -0.6% equity. Pack +0.30 (t=+0.9) insignificant.
Import-parity pricing in India and translation of European EBITDA lift INR profit; imported coal and USD/EUR debt offset. Net ~+4% EBITDA x1.4 x0.3-0.5.
Interest Rs7.1k cr TTM on ~Rs80k cr net debt; discount-rate channel on a levered cyclical.
Infrastructure/construction demand for Tata Steel India's long and flat products; +10% capex => ~+2.5% volume.
Largest Indian auto-steel supplier and key European auto supplier; +10% volume => +2% India flat volumes.

supply_chain.counterparty: Auto OEMs (Tata Motors group, Maruti etc.)
